problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 10 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 5 & 4 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. What are the dimensions of the eigenspaces ${V}_{3},$ ${V}_{1},$ and ${V}_{-2}$ corresponding to eigenvalues $\lambda =3,$ $\lambda =1,$ and $\lambda =-2$ of $A$, respectively?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069717/assets/442662066e9f90922c5113cad57faf1d735471da422963f8c19a7e09e6798c41.png)
Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. What are the dimensions of the eigenspaces $V_{0}$ and $V_{-2}$ corresponding to eigenvalues $\lambda=0$ and $\lambda=-2$ of $A$, respectively?
examples.worked_solution:
First, we write down the characteristic equation $\textrm{det}(A-\lambda I)=0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & -2-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ (-2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -3 \\ 1 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ (-2-\lambda )((1-\lambda )(-3-\lambda )+3)=0 \\ -(\lambda +2)({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda )=0 \\ \lambda (\lambda +2)^{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda_1=0$ (simple root) and $\lambda_2=\lambda_3=-2$ (double root). 

Let's now consider the eigenspaces corresponding to each eigenvector:

- First, we consider $\lambda=0.$ Since $V_{0}$ corresponds to a simple root, we obtain 

$$
\textrm{dim}(V_{0})=1.
$$

- Then, we consider $\lambda=-2,$ which is a repeated root of the characteristic equation. To find the dimension of $V_{-2},$ we row-reduce the matrix $(A - (-2) I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda = -2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\textrm{dim}(V_{-2})=2.
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 16 \\ -3 & 4 & -12 \\ 1 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}b \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2}$ shown above.
If ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are two linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2,$ what is the value of $a+b?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-2.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 16 \\ -3 & 4 & -12 \\ 1 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 & 16 \\ -3 & 6 & -12 \\ 1 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+16{x}_{3}=0 \\ -3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}-12{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 & 16 & 0 \\ -3 & 6 & -12 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & 6 & -12 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are free variables. On the other hand, from the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}.$ 

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

We now deduce the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

- Since ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we must have that ${x}_{2}=0$ and ${x}_{3}=1.$ As a result, $a=2(0)-4(1)=-4.$

- Since ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}b \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ we must have that ${x}_{2}=1$ and ${x}_{3}=0.$ As a result, $b=2(1)-4(0)=2.$

Therefore, $a+b=2-4=-2.$
